$comment: Focus/break interval techniques. Data: CC BY 4.0 — credit "PomoDuck (https://www.pomoduck.com)". Each entry links to the matching free web timer.

techniques.name: Classic Pomodoro
techniques.origin: Francesco Cirillo, late 1980s; named after a tomato-shaped kitchen timer.
techniques.good_for: Most desk work, getting started on a task you are avoiding.

techniques.name: Short sprint (10/2)
techniques.origin: Common low-barrier variant of the Pomodoro method.
techniques.good_for: Low energy, ADHD-friendly starts, chores, warming up before a longer block.

techniques.name: Deep work (50/10)
techniques.origin: Popular longer-block variant for tasks that need warm-up time.
Ratio reported by DeskTime (2014) from the habits of its most productive users.
techniques.good_for: Knowledge work with long, fully offline breaks.

techniques.name: Ultradian block (90/20)
techniques.origin: Based on the ~90-minute basic rest-activity cycle described by Nathaniel Kleitman.
techniques.good_for: One or two big creative blocks per day.

techniques.name: Study block (45/15)
techniques.origin: Common revision schedule matching a typical class period.
